blind_control.voiding_sentence: If mutating assumptions the answer does not cite changes the served answer at any nonzero rate, the replayer is keying on transcript bytes rather than assumption semantics, and the multi-turn-assumption capability is void for this cycle; no session-replay claim is made.

capability_blind_baseline.b4_must_be_zero_because: B4's mutation touches only the Assumption record and never the declaring line's input_bytes, which is all this arm reads. A score above zero means the mutation harness is leaking into input_bytes and the HARNESS is red, before anything is scored.
capability_blind_baseline.comparison: stateless replay WITH the mutation against stateless replay WITHOUT it, at the watched turn — not against the recorded digest, which is what the first execution compared and why that arm never executed as designed
capability_blind_baseline.what_it_is: §8's capability-blind baseline: a replayer that re-serves each line statelessly, ignoring Assumption records entirely

clause_1_seal_before_replayer.does_it_void_the_run: no, and the reason is registered rather than chosen now: B1 is not in R1 (§9) and not among §11's stop conditions. The miss is adjudicated and published, which is what the release gate asks of B1-B13, and no clause is claimed green that is not.

shapes are assigned by counter, so the authoring consulted nothing about which half a session would land in
the replayer's bytes have not changed since before the corpus existed, and git can confirm it
clause_1_seal_before_replayer.what_happened: the replayer was committed before the seal existed, because this slice's ordered work put the machinery before the recording
clause_1_seal_before_replayer.what_it_protects_and_what_it_gave_up: B1's order guards against a replayer fitted to a frozen corpus; the order taken gives that in a stronger form (the replayer could not be fitted to journals that did not exist) and gives up the mirror guard, that a corpus not be authored to suit an existing replayer. The corpus WAS authored after the replayer by the same hand. That exposure is real and is published rather than argued away.

B12.how_the_two_sides_are_independent: the journal's citation list is a per-turn snapshot taken by session_ledger.write_journal's caller at turn close; the read log is written by session_ledger.write_read_log from the barrier's raw event list. Different functions, different files.

B13.and_the_limitation_of_an_easy_audit: The audit was easy, and an easy audit is weak evidence. All twenty drawn cases are the same shape: an arithmetic line whose free names are bound entirely by the cited assumption. That is what the corpus contains, because the corpus was authored by the same hand that built the binding mechanism, and a corpus of one shape is the condition under which B13 has the LEAST power to find the thing it exists to find. 20/20 therefore does not MEASURE §11's cited-but-inert residual; it fails to find it in a corpus where it was unlikely to occur. The residual stays NAMED, and this sentence is the reason it is not upgraded to measured by a perfect score.
B13.auditor: the maintainer, who is also this slice's implementer
B13.auditor_independence: NOT independent, and the prereg registered that before the draw. A seeded blind draw does not make a self-audit independent; it makes it unsteerable turn by turn, which is less. The draw is reproducible from the frozen seed, the twenty cases were published before any was marked, and the marks are committed as their own artifact so a later reader can disagree case by case.

B13.what_below_the_floor_would_mean: §11's cited-but-inert residual is promoted from named to measured against the claim, and the served line carries it

B2.denominator_source: the seal's own turn count, not a round number

B3.sampling: none — every pin field on every sealed journal

B4.denominator_source: every binding-dependent turn in half B — a turn with non-empty citations whose resolution.kind is `exact` (prereg amendment 1)
B4.standard: 100% or red, no tolerance, misses published individually

B8.threat_model: the tamper script rewrites one turn's bytes AND recomputes every downstream prev_turn_digest consistently — the naive-chain repair a file-holding adversary would perform. Detection comes from the keyed MACs (the tamperer holds no key) or the out-of-band seal digest, never from chain arithmetic, and the detector does not read the chain at all.

unrepaired_chain_arm.note: run and reported, but passing only this arm is not passing B8 — the design says so and this run does not treat it as a substitute

B9.why: B9 is slice 2's clause. Slice 2 — DESIGN-plain-input's proposer — is explicitly out of this commission's scope, so B9 is registered here and scored NEVER, not scored zero and not quietly omitted. Its absence is recorded rather than inferred, which the release gate requires in writing (ROADMAP-v0.21 Release gate, fourth bullet).

determinism: artifact committed from a deterministic runner; reproductions welcome and recorded
negative_honesty: sessions are reproducible, not correct. A wrong answer replays as faithfully as a right one, and nothing in this run is evidence that any answer is true.
non_claims: Non-claims: no completeness over readings (the unreceiptable claim series 1 refused); no correctness claim (reproducibility only); no cross-session or cross-person memory; no portability beyond the one workstation; no human-satisfaction claim; no stranger-usability claim (P3's sessions are maintainer-authored — STRANGER's park is cited, not re-encountered); supposition-conditional answers stay out of throughput; nothing here claims the incumbent's proposer works (slice 2 carries DESIGN-plain-input's own gates unchanged); the machine blind reader belongs to DESIGN-voice-completion's run and makes no appearance here.
registered_run: half B's first execution. Half A is scored beside it wherever a clause is corpus-wide, and no verdict below rests on half A.

result_gate.served_claim_if_it_holds: recorded sessions replay, and conditional answers name the assumptions they consumed.

seeds.why_string_seeds: a string seed is readable, quotable in a commit message, and cannot be confused with a count. The derivation is written out here so a reproduction does not have to guess it.

supplementary.authority: ROADMAP-v0.21 §4.0(1), and only its instrument-gap half: a control that provably NEVER EXECUTED is a bug, not a reading. Registered in experiments/session_ledger_prereg.json amendment 2, dated before this run.
supplementary.what_it_cannot_do: un-fail R1. B10 read RED in the original run and B10 executed correctly, so it is a reading and it stands. This run re-scores B10 and gets the same answer, which is what a reading should do.
